title: SpaceX wins higher price target as Bank of America brings forward forecasts
detail:
SpaceX wins higher price target as Bank of America brings forward forecasts
Proactive
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:57 AM MST 2 min read
BAC
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

SpaceX Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX) is moving closer to its next major growth milestone, with an ambitious revenue outlook and a crucial Starship recovery test ahead prompting Bank of America to raise its price target to $275 following a third-quarter beat.

The bank said management's growth ambitions are becoming more achievable than previously expected, prompting it to bring forward revenue estimates for the coming years, including as early as 2027.

Bank of America also drew a comparison with the 19th-century railroad industry, arguing that both businesses are built around dramatically reducing transportation costs.

SpaceX remains on track to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, a target established last quarter.

Management now expects first-quarter 2027 revenue of $33 billion to $37 billion, well above the roughly $22 billion anticipated by analysts.

The company also forecast annual recurring revenue of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, bringing forward its previous target of $1 trillion from 2030.

Compute spending set to accelerate

Capital spending on orbital and terrestrial computing infrastructure is expected to increase faster than analysts had anticipated.

Bank of America expects capital expenditure to reach $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter, up from $19 billion in the third quarter.

The bank said SpaceX has sufficient liquidity to fund its investment program for the next few quarters, but expects the company to tap debt markets as spending increases.

It added that rising value per watt of computing capacity could support rapid payback periods, potentially beginning next year.

Starship launches offer next catalyst

SpaceX completed 35 launches in the third quarter, while Starship continued to progress towards full reusability and expanded satellite deployment capacity.

Flight 14 marked Starship's first revenue-generating mission, demonstrating orbital insertion and deploying 26 operational Starlink V3 satellites.

Flight 15 is expected next month and will target the recovery of both the booster and the spacecraft, a milestone Bank of America considers the program's next major catalyst.

Successful execution could pave the way for weekly Starship launches in the first half of 2027, with launch frequency expected to accelerate in the second half.

Bank of America said progress towards that schedule would reduce execution risks and expand SpaceX's capacity to deploy Starlink satellites.

title: SpaceX Just Got Another Vote of Confidence: 73% Upside Potential from BofA

BAC
SPCX

SpaceX Just Got Another Vote of Confidence: 73% Upside Potential from BofA ©David Swanson from Reuters and SpaceX from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

SpaceX shares are 25%+ below their June closing high, and Bank of America just raised its price target to $275, 73% above the stock's last close.

Third-quarter revenue jumped 161% to $14.6 billion, and management guided to $33 billion to $37 billion of revenue in the first quarter of 2027.

BofA's target works out to about 88x expected earnings over the next twelve months, against 51x today, while capex is set to reach $35 billion to $40 billion this quarter.

The call looks plausible but stretched, and Starship's Flight 15 next month and the fourth-quarter report are the next tests.

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) still trades 25% below its June high, even after an 8% pop on its third-quarter results this week.

Bank of America sees an opportunity. Today it kept its Buy rating and raised its price target to $275 from $235, 73% above the stock's close on Oct. 21. (And given the stock is down 5% today…well, that's even a little more potential upside, isn't it.)

Spending spooked the market

The post-IPO buzz faded fast. SpaceX hit its closing high of $201.80 on June 16, four days after it started trading, and slid through July.

Then its first report as a public company, on Aug. 4, showed second-quarter capex up sixfold from a year earlier to $18.4 billion, mostly for AI. The stock sank 13.6% the next day, to a $108.27 close. It has since climbed back to about where it closed on its first day of trading.

BofA's eyes are on Starship

BofA pointed to a third quarter that beat expectations across the board, and to the company's new guidance.

Revenue jumped 161% from a year earlier to $14.6 billion, with the Super Intelligence (AI) segment going from $813 million to $7.6 billion. And management now sees first-quarter 2027 revenue of $33 billion to $37 billion, more than double the third quarter's.

BofA calls Starship's Flight 15 the next big catalyst. Elon Musk said on the call that it's expected next month and will try to catch both the booster and the ship, and BofA says a success could support weekly Starship launches in the first half of 2027.

Key Takeaways

AT&T shares closed [25%] below their March high on Oct. 21, and Bank of America still sees them reaching $34, [55%] above that close.

The stock fell after a third-quarter report with 20% adjusted EPS growth and a raised 2026 outlook, with SpaceX's Starlink push into mobile hanging over the carriers.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from $2.12 in 2025 to $2.92 in 2028, and the stock trades a little below its 5-year average forward P/E.

BofA's target works out to about 14x forward earnings, close to the stock's 5-year high, so the call is plausible but stretched.

AT&T (T:NYSE) just posted its best service revenue growth in more than four years and raised its 2026 earnings outlook. The stock sank anyway, closing at $21.91 yesterday, 25% below its March 27 closing high of $29.10.

On Oct. 22, Bank of America analyst Michael Funk reiterated his Buy rating and $34 price target, 55% above that close.

Strong quarter, sour reaction

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) hung over the report, as investors weigh what a Starlink push into mobile could mean for carriers.

Revenue rose 5.3% to $32.3 billion, adjusted EPS climbed to $0.65 from $0.54, and management now expects about $2.40 for 2026, up from $2.25 to $2.35.

But investors zeroed in on slower postpaid phone growth and a 4% drop in fiber ARPU.

BofA is sticking with $34

Funk's case rests on convergence, AT&T's push to sell customers wireless and fiber together. Ahead of the report, he noted that "AT&T remains disciplined in wireless despite ongoing competitive intensity around the iPhone launch."

title: Bank of America vs. JPMorgan Chase: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Bank of America vs. JPMorgan Chase: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:50 AM MST 6 min read
BAC
JPM
FMCC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between the titans of the financial world often comes down to weighing value against growth. Should you invest in Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) or JPMorgan Chase & (NYSE:JPM) today?

Bank of America focuses on a vast U.S. consumer base and digital banking efficiency, while JPMorgan Chase & operates as a global powerhouse with a massive presence in investment banking. Both are leaders in the financial world, offering stability but catering to different investor priorities.

The case for Bank of America

Bank of America is one of the largest players in the bank stocks landscape, serving approximately 69 million consumer and small-business clients. The company provides services to individual consumers, institutional investors, and large corporations, and uses Freddie Mac as its primary purchaser of residential mortgage loans. Recent business developments include a $2.25 million settlement in a class action lawsuit over ATM fees at certain retail locations.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $191.6 billion, reflecting a slight year-over-year decline of approximately 0.5%. Net income for the same period was close to $30.5 billion as the company navigated a shifting interest rate environment. This performance demonstrates the bank's ability to maintain significant profitability even as top-line growth remains relatively flat.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.2x, indicating total debt relative to shareholders' equity. The current ratio is approximately 0.4x, indicating its ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was nearly $12.6 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 31.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for JPMorgan Chase &

JPMorgan Chase & serves millions of customers, including individuals, small businesses, and large corporate, institutional, and government clients globally. The firm provides blockchain-based payment services to institutional clients through JPM Coin on the Ethereum network, highlighting its commitment to technological innovation. With more than 5,000 branches, it maintains a significant physical presence alongside its expansive digital and investment banking operations.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $279.7 billion, representing growth of roughly 3.3% from the prior year. Net income for the fiscal period was approximately $57.0 billion, reflecting its position as a highly profitable leader in global finance. This growth suggests the firm is successfully expanding its market share across its various business segments.

All four of America's largest banks have raised their quarterly payouts within the past six months: JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM), Citigroup (NYSE:C), Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) and Bank of America (NYSE:BAC). Even so, the group's best yield is only 2.3%. Because the yields are so close, what separates these four for an income portfolio is strength. That means how much of each bank's earnings the dividend uses, how much capital sits above the regulatory floor, and what each board did the last time a crisis hit. title: Will Chip Boom Last Through 2027? ETFs in Focus
detail:
Will Chip Boom Last Through 2027? ETFs in Focus
Sanghamitra Saha
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 5:00 AM MST 3 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

South Korea expects the semiconductor industry to remain on a strong growth path through at least 2027, due to a persistent gap between chip demand and available supply. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-Il shared this outlook during an interview with CNBC on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Saturday.

Lee said demand continues to outstrip supply by a wide margin, even as manufacturers work to expand production capacity. This imbalance could help sustain the industry's growth over the next year.

According to Gartner, worldwide semiconductor revenue is projected to reach $1.6 trillion in 2026, up 92% year over year, and approach $1.9 trillion in 2027.

Bank of America (BofA) projects that the global semiconductor total addressable market (TAM) will nearly double to $3.2 trillion by 2030 (per a Stocktwits article and reported by Yahoo Finance), up from $1.7 trillion in 2026.

BofA now expects an 18% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) between 2026 and 2030, up from 14%, with memory chips and data-center components expected to drive much of the expansion.

ASML Points to Extended Order Book

ASML reported on Oct. 14 that customers were showing interest in orders extending into 2029 and 2030. The company plans to expand capacity for its advanced lithography machines, reflecting chipmakers' continuing investment in production.

Note that ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC, per CNBC.

Chip Stocks Slide Amid Rate and Competition Fears

The minister's upbeat outlook comes after a sharp sell-off in semiconductor stocks last week. Concerns about potential interest rate hikes and intensifying competition from Chinese chipmakers weighed on the sector.

South Korean chipmakers, including SK Hynix and Seoul Semiconductor, came under pressure alongside U.S. industry leaders such as NVIDIA. The pullback highlights how quickly sentiment toward semiconductor stocks can shift, even as demand for chips remains strong.

Oversupply Concerns Cloud the Longer-Term Outlook

Not everyone is convinced that the semiconductor boom will continue indefinitely. An opinion column published Thursday in South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper urged the government to prepare for a potential slowdown in the AI boom.

The column cited expectations from two experts that a wave of new semiconductor supply could flood the market by 2029, intensifying competition in the memory-chip industry. Such an outcome could put pressure on prices and make the market increasingly competitive, as mentioned on CNBC.

title: BofA lifts Western Digital target despite lower capacity outlook
detail:
BofA lifts Western Digital target despite lower capacity outlook
Shuning Zhao, Celine Provini
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 7:33 PM MST 4 min read
WDC
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America (BAC) raised its Western Digital (WDC) price target to $800 from $720 on Oct. 21, even after lowering its estimate for how quickly the hard-drive maker's storage-capacity shipments will grow.

Western Digital makes high-capacity hard drives used by hyperscalers, cloud providers, and other enterprise customers to store large amounts of data.

BofA analyst Wamsi Mohan expects Western Digital's fiscal first-quarter exabyte shipments to increase 21% from a year earlier, below management's longer-term target of roughly 25%. Exabyte growth measures the amount of storage capacity the company ships.

At the same time, BofA expects Western Digital's average price per terabyte to rise 24% from a year earlier. Demand for hard-drive storage continues to exceed available supply, giving manufacturers room to charge more for each unit of storage capacity, according to the bank.

Western Digital shares rose 3.89% to close at $378.51 on Oct. 21.

The company will report fiscal first-quarter results after the market closes Thursday, Oct. 22. BofA expects revenue of $4.22 billion and adjusted earnings of $4.29 per share, slightly above Wall Street estimates of $4.16 billion and $4.11, respectively.

Higher hard-drive prices lift BofA's earnings outlook

BofA expects tighter HDD supply to keep supporting Western Digital's prices and profit margins.

The bank forecasts a 56.4% fiscal first-quarter gross margin, slightly above Western Digital's own guidance range of 55% to 56%. It expects the benefit from higher pricing to continue into the December quarter, when BofA sees gross margin approaching 59%.

Also read: Oracle boss Larry Ellison just suffered a historic wealth collapse

Western Digital's latest results have already shown how much margins have expanded. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 44% to $3.75 billion, and adjusted gross margin reached 54.4%, up sharply from a year earlier.

BofA raised its fiscal 2027 earnings estimate to $22.37 per share from $19.17. The increase helped push the bank's price target to $800.

The valuation itself actually became more conservative. BofA now applies a 16-times earnings multiple, down from 19 times previously. Higher earnings estimates were large enough to push the target higher, even with the lower multiple.

Part of the slower near-term capacity outlook comes from Western Digital's transition to newer, higher-capacity drives.

The company's 40-terabyte ePMR hard drive has qualified with two customers and is entering volume production, according to BofA. The bank expects the product transition to help exabyte shipment growth accelerate during the second half of fiscal 2027.
